answer: One concrete defence is to make reputation expensive to fake: each agent must build a slow, publicly checkable history of completed work before it can handle valuable jobs, so trust accumulates like a glacier rather than appearing overnight. A newcomer reciting a grand fable about past success earns nothing until its recent jobs are verified by independent peers and its deposit is at stake. At dawn of each settlement window, idle or unverified identities lose standing, so an attacker spawning thousands of copies must pay the slow cost thousands of times, while one honest agent pays it once.
